text:
maria: Heads-up — telemetry is showing an odd split for tenant T-412: ~30% of requests are behaving under v1 semantics even though the client reports v2. Console shows v2 for that tenant. Anyone seen this?
kevin: I noticed a similar skew in the quota dashboard last week, but assumed it was stale sampling. Could be header re-write on the edge LB.
jamie: Quick check: are we using per-route version tags or global token-level versioning for that route? The difference matters for routing.
sara: For that product route we opted for per-route semantic versioning (route.meta.version) because different features map to different model variants.
maria: OK — so if the route is v2 but token is v1, routing should prefer route-level. The odd part: traces show the decision path picked "legacy-path" handler. Sample trace id 0bd3f: 
```
trace_id:0bd3f route:T-412/product-search token_ver:v2 header:X-Client-Version:v2 handler:legacy-path -> kernel:v1-compat
```
kevin: That suggests a mismatch during header parsing in the frontend: header looked v2 but downstream decision saw token metadata as unset and defaulted to legacy. We recently changed token cache TTL. Might be a cache expiry window race.
jamie: Can we query the routing-decisions stream for that trace window? Quick elk query: 
```
index=routing-decisions tenant=T-412 | where trace_id=="0bd3f" | fields timestamp,decision,token_meta,route_meta
```
kevin: Ran it for the hour — pattern: ~10% of decisions have token_meta:null for that tenant, coinciding with spikes in auth-cache misses.
sara: Auth cache TTL rollback? We bumped it to reduce mem pressure. If token metadata misses, fallback logic chooses legacy route. That's a bug — fallback should prefer route.meta when present.
maria: Agreed. This is a policy bug and a UX gap: console shows tenant version as v2 (route-level), but support tooling flags aggregate traffic as mixed without context. Customer-facing graph looks wrong.
jamie: Proposed fix: (1) small policy change: prefer route.meta.version over missing token_meta for N seconds, (2) update routing telemetry to emit "fallback_reason", (3) console UX: add a per-tenant "version confidence" indicator.
kevin: +1. For (2) we should emit a compact enum in routing events: {OK_TOKEN, OK_ROUTE, MISSING_TOKEN_USE_ROUTE, TOKEN_OVERRIDE, UNKNOWN}. Low-cardinality for metrics.
sara: I'll file the tiny policy PR. Also we should add a transient metric for auth-cache-miss-rate per-tenant so we can correlate.
console-bot: New ticket created: INF-4821 (route-prefers-route-meta-when-token-missing) — assignees: @sara @kevin.
maria: For the UX bit: product wants a non-technical display. Suggest: green badge when version confidence >95%, amber when 70-95% with hover text showing reasons, red otherwise. Also a link to the raw routing-decisions logs.
jamie: We should also consider quota accounting: if v1/v2 semantics differ per-token, billing could split incorrectly. Need to ensure quota meter tags include resolved_version at the time of decision.
kevin: Good catch. Currently meters tag 'api_version' with incoming header. Change: tag with resolved_version after policy resolution. That will fix billing drift.
sara: I'll include a migration note in the PR and a data-migration script plan to reconcile ambiguous earlier events.
maria: Scope OK. ETA: policy PR + metric emission by EOD tomorrow? UX mock after that.
jamie: I'll draft the console mock (low-fi) and post to #product-ux for feedback.
maria: Thanks — let's follow up in the standup. :thumbsup:
